content:
Alex Mendes: Heads up — after the routing-policy change yesterday I'm seeing heavy stutter on the main metrics viz. Panels hang for ~400-600ms on first interaction.
Maria Chen: Ugh. Reproable for you on prod only or locally too?
Alex Mendes: Prod only (reported by support). I can repro on canary when I enable the new routing header. :eyes:
Jordan Park: Any console/network logs? Could be backend streaming fallback to polling causing big UI churn.
Alex Mendes: Pasted perf trace: https://perf.redwood.example/trace/abc123 — main thread shows multiple full reflows around the chart mount
Sam Lee: Quick check — bundle size jumped in last deploy by ~180KB gzipped. Telemetry SDK went from 3.1.0 -> 3.2.0 in that PR (cc @Maria)
Maria Chen: I upgraded telemetry to get event sampling to ship. Didn't expect large diff. Where's the diff coming from?
Jordan Park: Likely telemetry is injecting wrapper props which change identity on every render. That will bubble into our chart painter causing re-renders.
Alex Mendes: I instrumented render counts — charts mount twice per route change now.
Eve (eng-sre): deploy-bot shows the last deploy: frontend@2024.11.14-37 (sha: d9f1c). Deployed 11:02 UTC.
deploy-bot: build artifacts: main-4a9c.js (1.8MB), charts-9b2f.js (420KB), telemetry-1c2d.js (210KB)
Sam Lee: Quick experiment: I disabled telemetry in browser devtools (window.__REDWOOD_TELEMETRY = false) — stutter disappears, renders go back to 1. So telemetry path is suspect.
Maria Chen: Sorry — the SDK change toggled autoBindProps by default. That's likely the cause.
Jordan Park: If telemetry is adding a new prop object each time, we can either memoize on provider level or stop passing full eventContext into chart components.
Alex Mendes: Repro snippet I used:
```
<MetricsChart data={normalizeSeries(raw)} eventContext={{ userId: uid, route: location.pathname }} />
```
normalizeSeries returns a fresh array each time (ok) but eventContext is created inline — telemetry wrapper was comparing shallow and forcing chart props to change.
Sam Lee: Fix plan:
- rollback telemetry SDK to 3.1.0 on canary (short-term) — Maria
- add memoization for eventContext in router provider (medium-term) — Sam
- create unit test to assert chart props stable across routing hops (longer-term) — Jordan
Maria Chen: I'll cut the rollback canary now and open a patch PR to disable autoBindProps by default. I'll also measure gzipped delta.
Eve (eng-sre): Noted. Routing policy change also flipped header order; that forced the telemetry shim to re-evaluate identity on hydrate in some cases.
Alex Mendes: For immediate mitigation we should also tweak webpack split to move telemetry into a separate async chunk so main bundle doesn't pick the full SDK upfront.
Sam Lee: Agreed. Split telemetry -> async chunk, add lazy load around observer. That should reduce initial main-thread parse/compile. I can prototype.
Jordan Park: I will own the test and follow-up with perf regression alert if bundle > +100KB gz.
Alex Mendes: Cool. Action items: Maria (rollback canary + PR), Sam (memoize + chunk split prototype), Jordan (tests + perf alert), Eve (monitor canary errors). I'll post perf numbers after next canary.
Maria Chen: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend/pull/4821 — reverting SDK to 3.1.0 for canary
Sam Lee: local patch to memoize eventContext:
```
const eventContext = useMemo(() => ({ userId: uid, route: location.pathname }), [uid, location.pathname]);
```
works to stop extra renders in my repro.
Eve (eng-sre): Monitoring: setting a 5m alert if first-paint latency increases > 150ms for dashboard route. I'll also watch error rates post-rollback.
Alex Mendes: Thanks team. If rollback doesn't fix it we'll triage deeper (heap snapshots etc). :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: Rolling back now. Will update thread when canary is green.
Alex Mendes: Update 11:30 UTC — canary rollback live, perf trace shows steady renders back to baseline. Leaving this open until split/memo PRs land.
Maria Chen: Filed follow-ups: frontend#786 (telemetry chunk split), frontend#787 (memoize provider), frontend#788 (perf test)
Jordan Park: Nice work — great quick detection. :rocket:
